{{Yearbox/in-conflicts}}
* [[Ches 28]]: [[Halisstra Melarn]], now [[Lolth]]'s Lady Penitent, begins attacking surface-dwelling [[drow]] in [[Cormanthor]] and the [[Dalelands]].<ref name="C.WAtT-p71">{{Cite dragon/Cormanthor: War Amidst the Trees|71}}</ref>
* [[Tarsakh 5]]: The red dragon [[Narlgathra]] attacks [[Tangled Trees]], killing almost all inhabitants.<ref name="C.WAtT-p71" /><ref name="GHotR-p153">{{Cite book/The Grand History of the Realms|153}}</ref>
* [[Tarsakh 12]]: Dragon hunters attack and destroy the [[Zhentarim]] garrison at [[Elmwood]] as well as three war galleys.<ref name="C.WAtT-p71" />
* [[Tarsakh 17]]: The black dragon [[Zarlandris]] attacks [[Highmoon]] and is killed, destroying the [[Tower of the Rising Moon]].<ref name="C.WAtT-p71" /><ref name="GHotR-p154">{{Cite book/The Grand History of the Realms|154}}</ref>
* [[Mirtul 2]]: [[Sammaster]], masquerading as [[Zhengyi the Witch-King]], uses a horde of [[orcs]] and [[giants]] in [[Vaasa]] to capture [[Bloodstone Pass]] and begin an invasion of [[Damara]].<ref name="GHotR-p154" />
* [[Mirtul 3]]: King [[Gareth Dragonsbane]] of Damara marches against the horde from Vaasa, but is betrayed by [[Cult of the Dragon]] loyalists in his ranks, and is banished to the [[Plane of Shadow]] for several weeks.<ref name="GHotR-p154" />
* [[Mirtul 25]]: The [[Monastery of the Yellow Rose]] in Damara is besieged by a number of chromatic dragons.<ref name="GHotR-p154" />
* [[Flamerule 11]]: [[Metallic dragon]]s relieve the siege of the Monastery of the Yellow Rose as Gareth Dragonsbane leads his forces against Sammaster's Vaasan horde.<ref name="GHotR-p154" /> The Vaasan monsters are routed after a ruse in which it is made to seem that Gareth kills the Witch-King.<ref name="tRite">{{Cite book/The Rite/MMP}}</ref>
* [[Uktar 13]]: The green dragon [[Verthandantalynx]] attacks and lays waste to the village of [[Trenahess]].<ref name="C.WAtT-p71" /><ref name="GHotR-p154" />
* [[Kaanyr Vhok]] and his Scoured Legion as well as the [[duergar]] of [[Gracklstugh]] attack [[Menzoberranzan]].<ref name="GHotR-p153"/><ref name="Condemn">{{Cite book/Condemnation/Paperback|?}}</ref>
* The [[Shou Lung]] Embassy in [[Elversult]] is destroyed by the storm drake [[Hathaulanyx]]. A scroll made of precious [[Ra-Khati]] vellum is recovered from its rubble. It bears the seal of the First Emperor Chin of the [[Ho Dynasty]], as well as his official proclamation canonizing the [[Organization of Thought]] in {{YearlinkConvert|581|SY}}.<ref name="TGHotR-42">{{Cite book/The Grand History of the Realms|42}}</ref>
* Using a magical globe stolen from the study of the late [[Thamalon Uskevren|Lord Thamalon Uskevren]], the [[Cyric]]ist [[shadow adept]] [[Vraggen]] locates the time and location where the [[Fane of Shadows]] will next appear on [[Toril]].<ref name="TF">{{Cite book/Twilight Falling}}</ref>
* Agents of Vraggen kill [[Sephris Dwendon]], [[Chosen]] of [[Oghma]], to stop him from helping [[Erevis Cale]], [[Jak Fleet]], and [[Drasek Riven]] from using the recovered globe to uncover the location of the Fane of Shadows. Undeterred, Erevis speaks with the man's spirit, who tells them the Fane will appear in the [[Moonmere]], in [[Gulthmere Forest]].<ref name="TF" />
* Arriving at the newly arrived Fane of Shadows, Erevis, Jak, and Drasek are too late to stop Vraggen. The Cyricist nearly succeeds in using the altar within the temple to transform into a [[shade]], but is killed by the [[slaad]] [[Azriim]], whom he thought was a [[half-drow]] ally. Stealing a sapling [[Weave Tap]] from the temple, Azriim and his allies escape. Erevis is nearly slain trying to save Jak, but saves himself by using the altar to turn himself into a shade.<ref name="TF" />
* Having survived the disappearance of the Fane of Shadows by being transported to the Plane of Shadow, Erevis and his companions eventually return to Toril only to discover that [[Vhostym]]'s slaadi are planning to use a seed from the Weave Tap to siphon power from the mantle protecting [[Skullport]]. They arrive too late, and Skullport is nearly destroyed.<ref name="DoN">{{Cite book/Dawn of Night|?}}</ref>
* [[Eltab]] returns from hiding and attempts to wrest control of the land of [[Thay]] from [[Szass Tam]] but is apparently defeated by [[Thazienne Uskevren]] in a titanic battle. In reality, ancient bindings by the [[Nar demonbinder|demonbinders]] of [[Narfell]] transported Eltab to the [[Citadel of Conjurers]] in [[Impiltur]] where he begins plotting his revenge anew.<ref name="CoR-132">{{Cite book/Champions of Ruin|132}}</ref>
* The surface city of [[Mirabar]] is devastated by [[Klauth]] but he is driven away before he can damage the undercity.<ref name="DoF-p43">{{Cite book/Dragons of Faerûn|43}}</ref>
* [[Leilon]] is engulfed in the poisonous breath of [[Voaraghamanthar]] and [[Waervaerendor]]. They kill half of that town's militia and the entire [[Cult of the Dragon]] cell based there.<ref name="DoF-p43"/>
* [[Skaug]] is ruined by [[Lhammaruntosz]] who also sinks around a dozen pirate vessels.<ref name="DoF-p43"/>
* The castle and many homes in [[Callidyrr]] are set aflame by [[Hoondarrh]] before he is driven off by a circle of [[druid]]s.<ref name="DoF-p43"/>
* [[Saelmur]] and [[Mintar]] enter a state of war. But [[Balagos]] sets fire to the cities, killing around half the population of each and leaving them both unable to field a large enough force to continue their war.<ref>{{Cite book/Dragons of Faerûn|42}}</ref>
* Three clans of [[Hartsvale]] [[giant]]s are slaughtered by [[Iymrith]].<ref name="DoF-p43"/>

{{Yearbox/births}}
* [[Ganrahast]], son of [[Myrmeen Lhal]] and [[Vangerdahast]]<ref>{{Cite dungeon/198/Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom|17}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/deaths}}
* [[Tarsakh 17]]: [[Zarlandris]] dies after attacking [[Highmoon]].<ref name="C.WAtT-p71" /><ref name="GHotR-p154" />
* [[Mirtul 22]]: [[Sirvinhandra]], the green dragon, attacks the [[Abbey of the Just Hammer]], causing devastation, and is killed by Lord High Justiciar High Avenger [[Deren Eriach]].<ref name="C.WAtT-p71" /><ref name="GHotR-p154" />
* [[Nightal 6]]: [[Sammaster]] the [[lich]] is destroyed to end the [[Rage of Dragons]].<ref name="GHotR-p154" />
* [[Bahamut]] is freed from his ancient prison.<ref name="GHotR-p154" />
* [[Iyraclea]], the Ice Queen who had long made the [[Great Glacier]] her home, perishes, beginning the inexorably slow melt of this great icy realm.<ref>{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|188}}</ref>
* [[Ryld Argith]] dies and his heart is eaten by his killer [[Jeggred Baenre]].<ref name=":0" />
* [[Belshazu]], the [[glabrezu]], father of Jeggred Baenre, is killed by Pharaun Mizzrym.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book/Annihilation/Paperback|?}}</ref>
* [[Pharaun Mizzrym]] dies in the [[Demonweb Pits]].<ref name="Resurrection">{{Cite book/Resurrection/Paperback|?}}</ref>
* [[Jeggred Baenre]] also dies in the Demonweb Pits.<ref name="Resurrection" />
* High King [[Keane]] of the [[Moonshae Isles|United Moonshaes]]. Attempts are made to [[Resurrection (spell)|resurrect]] him, but they fail.<ref name="Dr362-GHotR">{{Cite dragon/362/Grand History of the Realms: The Moonshaes|30}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/in-deities}}
* '''Ches 28:''' The [[Silence of Lolth]] ends.<ref name="C.WAtT-p71" />

{{Yearbox/in-people}}
* [[Hammer 1]]: [[Sammaster]] successfully ties his [[phylactery]] to the ''[[dracorage mythal]]'', separating the Rage of Dragons from the [[King-Killer Star]] and effectively causing all [[dragons]] to go mad.<ref name="DoF-p10">{{Cite book/Dragons of Faerûn|10}}</ref><ref name="GHotR-p153" /> Sammaster is later destroyed (on [[Nightal 6]]), ending the Rage of Dragons.<ref name="GHotR-p154" />
* The dragon-king [[Tchazzar]] returns to [[Chessenta]] and claims the crown.<ref name="Dun178">{{Cite dungeon/178/Backdrop: Chessenta|?}}</ref>
* [[Alustriel]] prevents [[Deszeldaryndun Silverwing]] and his mate [[Valamaradace]] from killing each other. In gratitude, they both pledge to defend [[Luruar]] from its enemies. Valamaradace is secretly named Alustriel's heir.<ref name="DoF-p42">{{Cite book/Dragons of Faerûn|42,44}}</ref>
* [[Mirtul 2]]: [[Pavel Shemov]] and [[Will Turnstone]] come to [[Hulburg]] to rescue the [[emerald dragon]] [[Vercevoran]] from the [[Zhentarim]] of the [[Citadel of the Raven]] and their summoned [[cerebrilith]].<ref name="tPoH">{{Cite book/Realms of the Dragons/The Prisoner of Hulburg|358–368}}</ref>
* Great Druid [[Robyn Kendrick]] returns from [[Faerie]] at the head of a circle of [[druid]]s who help to drive off Hoondarrh.<ref name="Dr362-GHotR" />

{{Yearbox/in-environment}}
* [[Kythorn 23]]: a plague known as [[Pox (plague)|the Pox]] burns through the human inhabitants of [[Hlondeth]].<ref name="GHotR-p154" />
* [[Eleasis 7]]: The red dragon [[Thraxata]] sets many fires in [[Battledale]], consuming a large part of the woodland there.<ref name="C.WAtT-p71" /><ref name="GHotR-p154" />
* [[Marpenoth 26]]:<ref name="GHotR-p154" /> [[Vhostym]] the Sojourner completes his greatest arcane work and pulls one of the larger [[tears of Selûne]] out of orbit. But he dies a day later and the tear plummets to the ground, fragmenting into thousands of flaming pieces.<ref>{{Cite book/Midnight's Mask/MMP|?}}</ref> This event becomes known as the [[Rain of Fire]] and is seen by tens of thousands of people, most of whom wrongly believe it was related to the Rage of Dragons.<ref name="GHotR-p154" />

{{Yearbox/in-organizations}}
* A failed mystical rite in which an abomination is weaned on the blood of a god drives the [[Rotting Man]] out of [[Dun-Tharos]] and raises hundreds of ancient demons in [[Dunwood|the Rawlinswood]] who slaughter all of the [[Talontar Blightlords]].<ref name="GHotR-p154" /><ref>{{Cite book/Lady of Poison|?}}</ref>
* The [[Blood of Morueme]] mindlessly slaughter their pureblooded [[hobgoblin]] relatives while their dragon masters are away. When the dragons return, they kill all of the surviving male hobgoblins, forcing the Blood of Morueme to perform the duties of the Red Flayers.<ref>{{Cite book/Dragons of Faerûn|89}}</ref>
* After becoming a [[dracolich]], [[Mornauguth]] begins a Cult of the Dragon cell based in the [[High Moor]] dedicated to the worship of [[Shar]].<ref name="DoF-p43"/>
* The [[half-dragon]]s of [[Battledale]] offer their services as guards to [[metallic dragon]]s in the [[Dalelands]] who intend to sleep through the Rage of Dragons. Rumors circulate among [[chromatic dragon]]s that they have a cure for the Rage, despite the half-dragons publicly refuting it. After [[Thraxata]] reacts badly to this news, the half-dragons organize themselves into the [[Sisterhood of Essembra]], trying to abate the devastation wrought by local dragonkind.<ref>{{Cite book/Dragons of Faerûn|98}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/misc}}
* [[Gaulauntyr]] destroys most of [[Nimpeth]]'s vineyards.<ref name="DoF-p43"/>
* Around a dozen dragons attack the [[Host Tower of the Arcane]]. They destroy the west tower and plunder it of [[magic]].<ref name="DoF-p42"/>
* [[Calathanorgoth]] sends his living relatives to the [[Serpent Hills]] where a ''[[King-Killer shield]]'' protects them from the Rage of Dragons.<ref>{{Cite book/Dragons of Faerûn|95-96}}</ref>
* A [[durzagon]] [[wizard]] of the [[Acolytes of the Hidden Flame]] discovers the ritual that will free [[Bazim-Gorag]] from the [[Dungeon of the Ruins]].<ref name="PotF-p17">{{Cite dungeon/101/Prison of the Firebringer|17}}</ref>
* This year is known as the Year of Madness in the [[Black Chronology]].<ref name="C.TotW-159">{{Cite book/Cormyr: The Tearing of the Weave|159}}</ref><ref name="TGHotR-157">{{Cite book/The Grand History of the Realms|157}}</ref>
* There were at least two [[vrock]]s serving [[Matron Mother]] [[Yasraena Dyrr]] of [[House Agrach Dyrr]] in [[Menzoberranzan]]. The vrocks were polymorphed as [[drow]] so as not to cause suspicion.<ref name="Res-p219">{{Cite book/Resurrection/Paperback|219}}</ref>

* '''1 Ches''': An [[orc]] warband accompanied by daemonfey launch an overnight attack on [[Rheitheillathor]] in the [[High Forest]]. Although the [[wood elf]] inhabitants fought back, they were forced into retreat.<ref name="FH-p101-105">{{Cite book/Forsaken House|101-105}}</ref>
* '''27 Ches''': The [[Battle of the Cwm]] sees the elves of [[Evereska]] and [[Evermeet]] victorious against the daemonfey armies, but not without heavy casualties.<ref name="FH-p214-227">{{Cite book/Forsaken House|214-227}}</ref>
* '''6 Tarsakh''': The army from [[Everlund]] led by [[Methrammar Aerasumé]] is ambushed in the [[High Forest]] by the daemonfey and accompanying orcs. The daemonfey and orcs are driven back, but only one [[fey'ri]] is killed in exchange for a larger number of casualties on the other side.<ref name="FH-p239-242">{{Cite book/Forsaken House|239-242}}</ref>
* '''22 Eleasias''': The crusading army of [[Evermeet]] combined with the forces of [[Sembia]] and the Dalelands defeat the fey'ri legion and retake the city of [[Myth Drannor]] in the name of the elves.<ref name="FG-p318">{{Cite book/Final Gate |318}}</ref>
* '''30 Uktar''': The [[Battle of Selgaunt]] is fought. The forces of Selgaunt repel the attackers.<ref name="GHotR-156-157">{{Cite book/The Grand History of the Realms|156-157}}</ref>
* '''1 Nightal''': The lich [[Priamon "Frostrune" Rakesk]] is defeated by [[Khelben "Blackstaff" Arunsun]], and teleported to [[Undermountain]] for [[Halaster Blackcloak|the Mad Mage]] to exact revenge on the Frostrune.<ref name="Blackstaff-p?" />
* '''1 Nightal''': [[Ordulin]], the capital of [[Sembia]], was mostly obliterated by a planar rift into the [[Shadow plane]] that opened in the skies above it, which allowed a pocket of the plane called the [[Adumbral Calyx]] to pour out. The rift was the result of the [[Shadowstorm]], brought forth by the [[Shar]]ran priestess [[Elyril Hraven]] using a ritual found in ''[[The Leaves of One Night]]''.<ref name="GHotR-157-158">{{Cite book/The Grand History of the Realms|157–158}}</ref>
* '''15 Nightal''': [[Shar]]ran assassins bypass the wards on [[Elminster]]'s tower and steal a [[Shadow Weave]] artifact called the ''[[Ebon Diadem]]''.<ref name="TGHotR-158">{{Cite book/The Grand History of the Realms|158}}</ref>
* '''16 Nightal''': In the early morning hours, the [[Zhentarim]] army led by [[Scyllua Darkhope]] overruns Shadowdale from the north. They are aided by the church of [[Shar]] and [[House Dhuurniv]] who attack the [[Twisted Tower]] from below. The [[Army of Myth Drannor]] is unable to respond as Zhentarim brigades to the east launch simultaneous attacks on several key elven fortifications.<ref name="S.TSotL-p4">{{Cite book/Shadowdale: The Scouring of the Land|4}}</ref><ref name="C.WAtT-p71">{{Cite dragon/Cormanthor: War Amidst the Trees|71}}</ref>
* The adventuring company known as [[Company of the Black Griffon]] searches the [[Wailing Tower]] for the treasure hoard of [[Aesperus]], the King in Copper. The seven adventurers barely escape with their lives.<ref name="TKiC">{{Cite book/Realms of the Dead/The King in Copper}}</ref>
* [[Church of Bane|Banite]] templars from [[Mourktar]] arrive to support the besieged [[Unther|Untheric]] city of [[Messemprar]]. The Banites, equipped with magical weaponry bought from [[Thay]] at a great discount, win several pivotal victories that halt the [[Mulhorand|Mulhorandi]] conquest.
* The [[Legion of Nanna-Sin]], an elite army of [[aasimar]], appears from nowhere and attacks the Mulhorandi army in the rear.
* The [[King of Shadows]] attacks the [[Sword Coast]] from the [[Plane of Shadows]].<ref>{{Cite game/Neverwinter Nights 2}}</ref>
* [[Fomorian]]s from [[Feywild|Faerie]] invade [[Oman's Isle]] and subjugate the [[firbolg]]s of the Grampalt Highlands. Together, they topple the Kingdom of [[Oman]] and conquer the entire island by Midsummer.<ref>{{Cite dragon/362/Grand History of the Realms: The Moonshaes|30}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/in-people}}
* [[Ususi Manaallin]] was able to find the entrance to the [[Celestial Nadir]] through the [[Mucklestone Gates]]. Where she, with the help of [[Imaskari vengeance taker|Vengeance Taker]] [[Iahn Qoyllor]], were able to stop an ancient Imaskar weapon. 
* [[Volothamp Geddarm]] journeys with a quartet of adventurers to the jungles of [[Samarach]] and is shipwrecked. A sect of [[yuan-ti]] devoted to the god [[Zehir]] attempts to overthrow the reigning yuan-ti royal family (devotees of [[Sseth]]).<ref>{{Cite game/Neverwinter Nights 2: Storm of Zehir}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/births}}
* [[Ganrahast]] is born to [[Myrmeen Lhal]]. [[Laspeera]] advises the Lord of [[Arabel]] to keep the identity of the child's father, [[Vangerdahast]], secret until he proves his magical ability. The boy is introduced at court as '''Ganrion'''<ref name="CR">{{Cite dungeon/198/Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom}}</ref>.

{{Yearbox/deaths}}
* [[Khelben Arunsun]] dies while restoring the city of [[Rhymanthiin]].<ref name="Blackstaff-p?" /> His title is inherited by [[Tsarra Chaadren]], who hides under [[illusion]]s to make it appear that Khelben is still the Blackstaff.<ref name="BT-p226">{{Cite book/Blackstaff Tower|226}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/in-deities}}
*Across [[Faerûn]], people flock to [[Elversult]] to convert to the Church of [[Amaunator]].<ref name="PoF-pg61">{{Cite book/Power of Faerûn|61}}</ref>
*The clergies of [[Cyric]] and [[Shar]] in [[Cormyr]] conspire to tear a hole in the [[Weave]] to create a vast [[Dead-magic zone]].<ref name="CTtotW-4">{{Cite book/Cormyr: The Tearing of the Weave|4}}</ref>
*[[Mask]] surrenders himself to Shar, who absorbs his essence, resulting in Mask's death.<ref name=TTW-330-333">{{cite book/Shadowrealm|330-333}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/in-politics}} 
* '''10 Ches''': [[Seiveril Miritar]] resigns from Evermeet's ruling council.
* [[Imbrar II]] becomes king of [[Impiltur]].
* '''26 Kythorn''': [[Hillsfar]] breaks its alliance with [[House Dlardrageth]]. In response, the fey'ri attack the [[Red Plumes]] and destroy the First Lord's Tower, forcing [[Maalthiir]] into hiding.
* [[Alusair Obarskyr]], responding to pressure from her nobles, declares that all of [[Cormyr]]'s roads will now be maintained by the Crown instead of the owners of the land they run through.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://dnd.wizards.com/articles/features/skalantur-scandal |title=The Skalantur Scandal |accessdate=2016-03-29 |author=[[Ed Greenwood]] |authorlink= |coauthors= |date=2014-02-11 |format=HTML |work=Forging the Realms |publisher=[[Wizards of the Coast]] |pages= |language= |archiveurl= |archivedate= |quote= }}</ref>

{{Yearbox/misc}}
* The whole continent of Faerûn is beset by an unusual year-long rain of [[meteor]]s and lightning storms. In a series of visions, [[Bahamut]] and [[Tiamat]] instruct their followers to seek out the impact points of the meteors, as each contains some form of dragon egg. Although Bahamut's followers have the help of the [[Sisterhood of Essembra]] to recover the eggs that land on the [[Dalelands]], members of the [[Church of Tiamat]] are more effective in retrieving most of the eggs. They bring back more than half to the Altar of Scales in [[Unthalass]], in preparation for a possible new battle of the [[Dragonfall War]]. The rest of the eggs are recovered by Bahamut's followers, hatch on their own, or are lost.<ref name="tGHotR-p154">{{Cite book/The Grand History of the Realms|154}}</ref><ref name="DoF">{{Cite book/Dragons of Faerûn|10,98}}</ref>
* [[Alturiak 16]]: [[Sarya Dlardrageth]] uses the [[Gatekeeper's Crystal]] to dispel the magical protection on [[Nar Kerymhoarth]] and gains access, freeing nearly two-thousand fey'ri.<ref name="FH-p55-56">{{Cite book/Forsaken House|55-56}}</ref>
* Reverent Dreamer [[Rhistel Laelithar]]'s ''[[Treatise Historical of the Dragon Tyrants]]'' is recovered from the ruins of [[Myth Drannor]].<ref name="TGHotR-9">{{Cite book/The Grand History of the Realms|9}}</ref>
* [[Eratharn]] of [[Candlekeep]] writes ''[[The Kingdoms of Men: A Guide to the Great Rulers]]'' about [[human|humanity's]] history on [[Toril]].<ref name="TGHotR-74">{{Cite book/The Grand History of the Realms|74}}</ref>
* Cragwarden [[Samiel Tussin]] unearths two [[runestone]]s from the sands of [[Itzcala]], just southwest of [[Trythosford]]. The translated text from them describes the [[Rockfire Disaster]] of [[987 DR]].<ref name="TGHotR-114">{{Cite book/The Grand History of the Realms|114}}</ref>
* The young [[bard]] [[Elender Stormfall]] publishes the chapbook ''[[The Dream of the Dragon]]'', an excerpt of which describes the first few days after the death of [[Azoun IV]].<ref name="TGHotR-152">{{Cite book/The Grand History of the Realms|152}}</ref>
* Three agents of [[House Thorp]] are murdered by burnt [[ossra]] oil. The [[Lords of Waterdeep]] ban all such substances from the city.<ref>{{Cite dungeon/127/Vampires of Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Crypt|72}}</ref>
* The religious dilettante Lord [[Thestus Thongolir]] is kidnapped by agents of the [[Xanathar Thieves' Guild]] working for Lord [[Ulguth Ilvastarr II]] after Thestus changes his mind about helping Ulguth set up a cult to [[Gargauth]] in [[Waterdeep]].<ref>{{Cite dungeon/127/Vampires of Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Crypt|72}}</ref>
* [[Dhusarra yr Fadila el Abhuk]] leads a force of [[Uthgardt]] [[Gray Wolf tribe]] [[vampires]] into Waterdeep on a [[High Hunt]] for [[Artor Morlin]]. She and her servants are overmatched.<ref>{{Cite dungeon/126/Vampires of Waterdeep: Blood of Malar}}</ref>
* This year is known as the Year of the Unraveling in the [[Black Chronology]].<ref name="C.TotW-159">{{Cite book/Cormyr: The Tearing of the Weave|159}}</ref><ref name="TGHotR-157">{{Cite book/The Grand History of the Realms|157}}</ref>
* On the [[Feast of the Moon]], a High Magic Ritual of Myriad is performed to restore [[Faer'tel'miir]], the Library City of [[Miyeritari]], as the renamed city of [[Rhymanthiin]], the Hidden City of Hope, in the [[High Moor]]. [[Khelben Arunsun]] gives his life to help make the ritual's magic permanent.<ref name="Blackstaff-p?" />
* Following victory over the King of Shadows, the [[Kalach-Cha]] is transported halfway across Faerûn to the country of [[Rashemen]] and comes under the influence of a curse called the [[Spirit-eater]].<ref>{{Cite game/Neverwinter Nights 2: Mask of the Betrayer}}</ref>

** [[Vhaeraun]] is killed by his sister, [[Eilistraee]], when he attempts to enter her realm and assassinate her. The Dark Maiden temporarily gains his portfolio, and temporarily takes the title of Masked Lady alongside her previous ones.<ref name="GHotR-158">{{Cite book/The Grand History of the Realms|158}}</ref><ref group="note">''[[The Grand History of the Realms]]'' explicitly says that Vhaeraun's assassination attempt failed and Eilistraee killed him. However, in [http://forum.candlekeep.com/topic.asp?TOPIC_ID=19841&whichpage=22#476639 one of his answers], [[Ed Greenwood]] suggests that Eilistraee actually spared her brother's life. The Dark Maiden defeated Vhaeraun with the indirect help of her ally [[Mystra (Midnight)|Mystra]], as the [[Weave]] frustrated the Masked Lord's magic while enhancing Eilistraee's. The goddess temporarily took her brother's portfolio, and trapped his sentience in the Weave, where it was enfolded in a dream by Mystra. The Lady of Mysteries did that to ensure that the two drow siblings would survive the cataclysm that she knew was coming—the [[Spellplague]]—in which she would be "killed" to renew the Weave, and magic would go wild. After Mystra and the Weave were completely restored in 1487 DR, the goddess of magic could finally give Eilistraee her own lost power and do the same with Vhaeraun, after having awakened him from his dream.</ref>

{{Yearbox/in-environment}}
* The seasons continue to start and end later than normal as a result of the environmental chaos of the separation of [[Abeir]] from [[Toril]] in the prior years. While some fear this change is permanent, most expect the seasons to return to normal in the coming years.<ref name="SCAG-p15">{{Cite book/Sword Coast Adventurer's Guide|15}}</ref>
* In [[Icewind Dale]], the nonstop two-year winter of [[Auril]]'s [[Everlasting Rime]] ends.<ref name="IDRotFm-p5"/><ref group="note">Aside from being the date identified in ''[[Icewind Dale: Rime of the Frostmaiden]]'' (pp. 5), the fact that the Everlasting Rime is not mentioned in other materials released for [[Dungeons & Dragons]] 5th edition which mention or visit [[Icewind Dale]] during or after 1489 DR (such as the ''[[Sword Coast Adventurer's Guide]]'', ''[[The Rise of Tiamat]]'' and ''[[Storm King's Thunder]]'') suggests that the Rime was meant to end in 1489 DR.</ref>

{{Yearbox/migrations}}
* The rebellion against the rule of Vorgansharax, having failed, causes Phlan's refugees to flee to [[Mulmaster]].<ref name="CS1"/>

{{Yearbox/in-people}}
* [[Severin Silrajin]], under orders from [[Tiamat]], attempts to create the ''[[Mask of the Dragon Queen]]'' to free her from the [[Nine Hells]] and collect a treasure hoard that she might deem worthy.<ref name="HotDQ"/>{{ToD-time}}
* The dragon [[Throstulgrael]] achieves [[dracolich]]dom.<ref name="CS1"/>
* [[Tyranthraxus]] returns to the Realms through a newly unearthed ''[[pool of radiance]]'' and possesses the body of Vorgansharax.<ref name="CS1"/><ref>{{Cite adventurers league/Pool of Radiance Resurgent}}</ref>
* [[Ammalia Cassalanter|Ammalia]] and [[Victoro Cassalanter]] sign a pact with [[Asmodeus]] trading their children's souls in exchange for financial prosperity. Their eldest son, [[Osvaldo Cassalanter|Osvaldo]], is immediately taken, his body transformed into a [[chain devil]].<ref name="WDH5e-p116">{{Cite book/Waterdeep: Dragon Heist|116}}</ref>{{Waterdeep-time}}
* The adventurer [[Harko Swornhold]] is exiled from Waterdeep for attempting to bribe a magistrate.<ref name="WDH5e-p38">{{Cite book/Waterdeep: Dragon Heist|38}}</ref>
* [[Arrant Quill]], a heroic [[bard]] in service to the [[Harpers]], is corrupted by a magic item imbued with the power of [[Cyric]], causing him to turn against his old allies. His Harper friends respond by imprisoning him in a [[Wisteria Vale (demiplane)|demiplane]] concealed within a book called ''[[The Curious Tale of Wisteria Vale]]'' while they attempt to research a cure. The book is donated to [[Candlekeep]] that same year for safekeeping and for access to the library's knowledge.<ref name="CM-p155">{{Cite book/Candlekeep Mysteries/The Curious Tale of Wisteria Vale|147-148,155}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/in-politics}}
* The Harpers form a pact with the [[fey]] of Kryptgarden forest serving [[Witchthorn|King Witchthorn]], an Unseelie lord.<ref name="CS1"/>
* A variety of new priesthoods spring up across the Realms to discern the will of the gods in the wake of the [[Second Sundering]].<ref name="SCAG-p18">{{Cite book/Sword Coast Adventurer's Guide|18}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/misc}}
* Three merchant ships are mysteriously obliterated near [[Luskan]], prompting [[Jarlaxle]] and his allies to investigate.<ref name="OEJ">{{Cite book/One-Eyed Jax: A Forgotten Realms Adventure}}</ref>
* The [[Lantan]]ese [[submarine]] ''[[Scarlet Marpenoth]]'' is launched.<ref name="WDH5e-p46">{{Cite book/Waterdeep: Dragon Heist|46}}</ref>
* The [[nautiloid]] ''[[Id Ascendant]]'' crashes in southern [[Icewind Dale]], stranding a crew of two [[gnome ceremorph]]s and three [[gnome squidling]]s, as well as a complement of otherworldly pets and living experiments, in the icy region.<ref name="IDRF5e-p132-137">{{Cite book/Icewind Dale: Rime of the Frostmaiden|132-137}}</ref>

{{LunarCalendarBox}}

{{Yearbox/in-conflicts}}
* A conflict between the [[Xanathar's Thieves' Guild]] and the [[Zhentarim]] in [[Waterdeep]] escalates into a street war.<ref name="WDH5e-p5">{{Cite book/Waterdeep: Dragon Heist|5}}</ref>{{Waterdeep-time}}
* A skirmish between members of the Zhentarim and the [[Gralhund]] family becomes known by [[Waterdeep|Waterdhavian]] broadsheets as the [[Gralhund Villa Bloodbath]].<ref name="WDH5e-p56">{{Cite book/Waterdeep: Dragon Heist|56}}</ref>
* The city of [[Elturel]] is pulled into the first layer of the [[Nine Hells]], [[Avernus]], leaving nothing behind but a crater.<ref name="BGDA-p5">{{Cite book/Baldur's Gate: Descent into Avernus|5-8}}</ref>{{BG-DiA-time}} The city is saved by brave heroes and returns to its former location before the end of the year.<ref name="HoF-p81">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Heroes of Faerûn|81}}</ref><ref name="BG3" />
* The library of [[Candlekeep]] is attacked by the [[Order of the Immortal Lotus]], who kill two acolytes and steal dangerous secrets by tearing pages from ''[[The Book of Inner Alchemy]]''.<ref name="CM-p160">{{Cite book/Candlekeep Mysteries/The Book of Inner Alchemy|160-161}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/in-organizations}}
* A [[clone]] of [[Manshoon]] appears in Waterdeep and strives to exert control over the local Zhentarim from his base at [[Kolat Towers]].<ref name="WDH5e-p7">{{Cite book/Waterdeep: Dragon Heist|7}}</ref><ref name="WDH5e-p17">{{Cite book/Waterdeep: Dragon Heist|17}}</ref>
* Waterdeep's [[City Watch (Waterdeep)|City Watch]] is overwhelmed by violence throughout the city,<ref name="WDH5e-p38">{{Cite book/Waterdeep: Dragon Heist|38}}</ref> leading to factions stepping in to help fight gangs and monsters, including the [[Emerald Enclave]], the [[Harpers]], the [[Lords' Alliance]], the [[Order of the Gauntlet]], and even the [[Zhentarim]].<ref name="WDH5e-p35">{{Cite book/Waterdeep: Dragon Heist|35,37-40}}</ref>
* Cultists of the [[Dead Three]] based out of the [[Hamhocks Slaughterhouse]] in [[Baldur's Gate]]'s [[Baldur's Gate/Outer City|outer city]] go on a murder spree throughout the city. They dump the bodies of their victims behind the [[Smilin' Boar]].<ref name="BG:DiA-p197">{{Cite book/Baldur's Gate: Descent into Avernus|197}}</ref><ref name="BG:DiA-p20">{{Cite book/Baldur's Gate: Descent into Avernus|11,20}}</ref>
* The [[Amberdune Pack]] of [[jackalwere]]s is driven from their home in [[Amn]] when their leader, [[Nidalia]], is slain. After a few months, they hatch a scheme to pay to ''[[Resurrection (spell)|resurrect]]'' her in Baldur's Gate by creating and selling [[gingwatzim]]s disguised as valuable books.<ref name="CM-p27">{{Cite book/Candlekeep Mysteries/Mazfroth's Mighty Digressions|27}}</ref>
* The [[Scarlet Sash]], an order of [[wereraven]]s dedicated to stealing potent [[magic items]] away from evil individuals, acquires a desecrated ''[[Figurine of Orcus]]'' before it can be sold at an auction.<ref name="CM-p37,44">{{Cite book/Candlekeep Mysteries/Book of the Raven|37,44}}</ref>
* The [[Burnt Tongue Cult]] begins kidnapping travelers along the [[Trade Way]] between Waterdeep and [[Daggerford]].<ref name="CM-p105">{{Cite book/Candlekeep Mysteries/Sarah of Yellowcrest Manor|105-106}}</ref>
* A cult known as the [[Livestock (cult)|Livestock]] hatch a scheme to launch one of the towers of Candlekeep into [[wildspace]]. When their secret is betrayed by [[Buron Sternmettle|one of their own]], they move up their timetable and cause an earthquake.<ref name="CM-p124">{{Cite book/Candlekeep Mysteries/Kandlekeep Dekonstruktion|124-125}}</ref>
* The Harpers devise a means to cure their former member, [[Arrant Quill]], of evil corruption, but must first confront him within the [[Wisteria Vale (demiplane)|demiplane]] in which they trapped him three years prior. At the same time, a [[beholder]] named [[Renekor]] dreams itself into the demiplane and imprisons Arrant.<ref name="CM-p148">{{Cite book/Candlekeep Mysteries/The Curious Tale of Wisteria Vale|148}}</ref>
* The [[Cult of the Absolute]] rises, in which followers worship [[the Absolute]], a so-called god that they believe is destined to take over the world, leading to a new order where [[True Soul]]s rule above all else.<ref name="BG3">{{Cite game/Baldur's Gate III}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/in-people}}
* [[Victoro Cassalanter|Victorio]] and [[Ammalia Cassalanter]] seek to buy their way out of their infernal contract with [[Asmodeus]] in order to save the souls of their children, [[Elzerina Cassalanter|Elzerina]] and [[Terenzio Cassalanter|Terenzio]].<ref name="WDH5e-p115">{{Cite book/Waterdeep: Dragon Heist|115}}</ref>
* Agents of the Zhentarim and of Xanathar's Thieves' Guild vie to kidnap [[Renaer Neverember]] as they believe he knows how to use the ''[[Stone of Golorr]]''. They accidentally take his lookalike, [[Floon Blagmaar]], instead.<ref name="WDH5e-p26">{{Cite book/Waterdeep: Dragon Heist|26}}</ref>
* The [[ghost]] of a girl named [[Sarah]] manifests in Candlekeep alongside her journal, which seems to detail disturbing information about Lord [[Viallis Yellowcrest]] of Waterdeep.<ref name="CM-p100">{{Cite book/Candlekeep Mysteries/Sarah of Yellowcrest Manor|100-101}}</ref>
* A young [[bronze dragon]] named [[Zelifarn]] takes up residence in the [[Waterdeep Harbor]].<ref name="WDH5e-p36">{{Cite book/Waterdeep: Dragon Heist|36}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/in-politics}}
* [[Jarlaxle]] seeks leverage over members of the [[Lords' Alliance]] in hopes of pressuring them to admit [[Luskan]] onto their council.<ref name="WDH5e-p6">{{Cite book/Waterdeep: Dragon Heist|6}}</ref>
* [[Dagult Neverember]] sends agents to Waterdeep in hopes of reclaiming the half a million [[currency|gold dragons]] he embezzled during his tenure as [[Open Lord]].<ref name="WDH5e-p5"/><ref name="WDH5e-p43">{{Cite book/Waterdeep: Dragon Heist|43}}</ref>
* Grand Duke [[Ulder Ravengard]] of Baldur's Gate disappears during a diplomatic visit to [[Elturgard]] when he is taken to Avernus along with Elturel. This leaves the [[Flaming Fist]] without a leader, so Duke [[Dillard Portyr]] recalls his niece, [[Liara Portyr]], from [[Chult]] in order to take command of the mercenary army.<ref name="BG:DiA-p10">{{Cite book/Baldur's Gate: Descent into Avernus|10}}</ref> 
* Upon his return to the [[Prime Material plane|Prime Material Plane]], Grand Duke Ulder Ravengard is captured by Absolute cultists and taken to [[Moonrise Towers]], where he is infected with an [[Mind flayer|illithid]] tadpole and becomes the puppet of [[Enver Gortash]]. He announces Gortash as the first Archduke of Baldur's Gate.<ref name="BG3" />

{{Yearbox/migrations}}
* A flood of refugees arrive in Baldur's Gate from Elturgard following the disappearance of Elturel.<ref name="BG:DiA-p10"/> In response, the city bars its outer gates against them.<ref name="BG:DiA-p11">{{Cite book/Baldur's Gate: Descent into Avernus|11}}</ref>
* A group of [[yuan-ti]] followers of the [[Scaled Mother]] leave [[Chult]] and arrive peacefully at a [[grippli]] village in the [[Cloak Wood]] on the [[Sword Coast]], where they begin excavating what they believe to be a temple to their deity. They are shortly followed by a much more murderous group of yuan-ti, who capture the first group and seize control of the grippli village.<ref name="CM-p92">{{Cite book/Candlekeep Mysteries/Book of Cylinders|92}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/in-deities}}
* The [[mummy lord]] [[Valin Sarnaster]] of the [[House of the All-Seeing Orb]] in [[Tashluta]] schemes to usurp [[Savras]]. She enacts a plan to transform her enemies into [[canopic golem]]s to prevent them from interfering.<ref name="CM-p172">{{Cite book/Candlekeep Mysteries/The Canopic Being|172-174}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/in-environment}}
* The [[saprophytic plague]] ravages the Sword Coast, causing [[disease]] and famine on a massive scale.<ref name="CM-p213">{{Cite book/Candlekeep Mysteries/Xanthoria|213}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/deaths}}
* [[Dalakhar]], a [[rock gnome]] in service of Lord Dagult Neverember of Neverwinter, is killed by a ''[[fireball]]'' in [[Trollskull Alley]] in Waterdeep.<ref name="WDH5e-p43" />
* Duke [[Dillard Portyr]] of Baldur's Gate is assassinated.<ref name="DotD-p3">{{Cite adventurers league/Day of the Devil|3}}</ref> He gets better.<ref name="AiF-p192">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|192}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/misc}}
* A series of individuals go missing from Candlekeep, including a visiting sage named [[Matreous]],<ref name="CM-p17">{{Cite book/Candlekeep Mysteries/The Joy of Extradimensional Spaces|17}}</ref> an acolyte named [[Falthrax Loderr]],<ref name="CM-p75">{{Cite book/Candlekeep Mysteries/The Price of Beauty|75-76}}</ref> and a scholar named [[Mayastan Sadaar]].<ref name="CM-p170">{{Cite book/Candlekeep Mysteries/The Canopic Being|170}}</ref>
* In Baldur's Gate, several merchants and [[Nobility of Baldur's Gate|patriars]] attempt to strong-arm the owners of the shop [[Distant Shores]] into selling their business.<ref name="BG:DiA-p179">{{Cite book/Baldur's Gate: Descent into Avernus|179}}</ref>
* A [[magical]] book called ''[[Shemshime's Bedtime Rhyme]]'' causes a [[curse]] to spread in Candlekeep, causing all those infected to be unable to resist humming a specific nursery rhyme. The [[Avowed]] quarantine the cursed individuals beneath the [[House of Rest]].<ref name="CM-p61">{{Cite book/Candlekeep Mysteries/Shemshime's Bedtime Rhyme|61-62}}</ref>
* A pair of [[bedine]] nomads—[[Pesh]] and [[Shamir]]—discover the [[Sapphire Sentinel]] not far from [[Haruun]].<ref name="CM-p200">{{Cite book/Candlekeep Mysteries/Alkazaar's Appendix|200-202}}</ref>

* A contingent of the [[Flaming Fist]] launches an attack on murderous [[Dead Three]] cultists at the [[Hamhocks Slaughterhouse]] in [[Baldur's Gate]]'s [[Baldur's Gate/Outer City|Outer City]], bringing them to justice.<ref name="AiF-p208">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|208}}</ref>
* [[Sahuagin]] led by Baron [[Skurr]] prepare to raid Baldur's Gate to recover a sacred [[conch]].<ref name="AiF-p207">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|207}}</ref> Sahuagin begin covert attacks around the docks, launched from an abandoned ship called the ''[[Fearsome Grimace]]''.<ref name="AiF-p222">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|222}}</ref>
* A long-frozen [[beholder]] emerges from the mines of [[Termalaine]] in [[Icewind Dale]] and goes on a destructive rampage.<ref name="AiF-p127">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|127}}</ref>
* [[Szass Tam]], having lost total control over the [[Council of Zulkirs]], plots to destroy them and reestablish himself as sole ruler of [[Thay]] using a ritual known as ''[[Malefice Mortum]]''. His plans are discovered by spies of [[Zulkir]] [[Xelnene Thrul]], who launches [[Operation Deadfall]] to thwart him.<ref name="AUD-p33">{{Cite book/Arcana Unleased: Deadfall|33}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/deaths}}
* [[Krazbrax Nixel]], who requests on his deathbed that adventurers travel through the [[time gate]] at [[Fool's Needle]] to prove that it leads to ancient [[Netheril]].<ref name="NF">{{Cite web/D&D Beyond/Netheril's Fall}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/in-deities}}
* Statues representing five "forgotten" [[deities]] awaken and cause havoc in [[Calimport]]'s [[Temple of a Thousand]]. These include the [[Hukh]], [[Korus]], [[Motanwe]], [[Nimbus]], and [[Sholoban]].<ref name="AiF-p157">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|157}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/in-environment}}
* The [[Rusting]] appears in the harbor and along the coast near [[Kythyss]] on the southern tip of [[Alaron]] in the [[Moonshae Isles]].<ref name="AiF-p187">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|187}}</ref>
* An outbreak of the [[Shaking Plague]] strikes [[Scardale Town]]'s docks and slums.<ref name="AiF-p35">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|35}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/in-organizations}}
* [[The Guild]] takes control of the Hamhocks Slaughterhouse, turning it into their largest operation outside of Baldur's Gate's [[Baldur's Gate/Lower City|Lower City]].<ref name="AiF-p208" />
* The Guild scrambles to eliminate inventor [[Flurn Eightspoke]] after he unknowingly creates a [[clockwork]] copy of the mind of one of their informants.<ref name="AiF-p224">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|224}}</ref>
* A cult of [[Auril]] led by [[Nymetra|Ice-Knife Nymetra]] operates out of [[Caer-Dineval]] and begins to capture inhabitants of [[Easthaven]] to sacrifice to their goddess. Easthaven's sheriff, [[Markham Southwell]], takes notice after the disappearance of a fisherman named [[Bott Witters]].<ref name="AiF-p110,124">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|110-111,124}}</ref>
* A [[Zhentarim]] caravan transporting stolen goods from [[Bryn Shander]] to [[Targos]] is attacked by cultists from [[Dougan's Hole]].<ref name="AiF-p126">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|126}}</ref>
* Members of the [[patriar]] [[Eomane]] family host a lavish party with the intention of killing the guests for the glory of [[Bhaal]].<ref name="AiF-p223">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|223}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/in-people}}
* The [[specter]] of the [[ogre]] warlord [[Bonegnasher]] grows restless in the [[Tomb of Damara]], and kidnaps the [[Silverstar (family)|Silverstar]] family from [[Shadowdale Town]] after [[Sara Silverstar]] finds the key to the Tomb.<ref name="AiF-p86">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|86}}</ref>
* [[Vargrazt|Vargrazt the Wretch]] proposes to purify the remains of the crashed [[chardalyn dragon]] in Easthaven via a [[ritual]].<ref name="AiF-p125">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|125}}</ref>
* The [[lamia]] [[Selim (lamia)|Selim]] plots to steal a ''[[brazier of commanding fire elementals]]'' from the [[Calishite]] merchant [[Shezar Han]].<ref name="AiF-p156">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|156}}</ref>
* The performer [[Braelin Wyngard]] is captured by a [[night hag]] while exploring a [[wandering isle]] near the Moonshae Isles.<ref name="AiF-p188">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|188}}</ref>
* The [[gnome]] [[scholar]] [[Vigglestern]] discovers a time gate leading to the city of [[Conch (city)|Conch]] during the last years of the ancient Netherese empire.<ref name="NF" />

{{Yearbox/in-politics}}
* The [[Dales Council]] seeks capable new leaders to rebuild [[Freedale]].<ref name="AiF-p87">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|87}}</ref>
* High King [[Derid Kendrick]] of the [[United Moonshae Isles|Moonshae Isles]] seeks a formal peace treaty with [[Thuven Moltenbeard]], the [[fire giant]] king of [[Oman's Isle]]. The High King sends emissaries, but a [[fomorian]] known as [[Ulrik Fellwhisper]] works to sabotage the talks.<ref name="AiF-p189">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|189}}</ref>
* Jarl [[Olfsvenn]] of [[Norland (kingdom)|Norland]] learns the location of the lost [[ring]] of [[Cymrych Hugh]], and seeks to acquire it for High King Derid Kendrick.<ref name="AiF-p189" />
* Followers of [[Bane]] who had infiltrated Baldur's Gate's [[Parliament of Peers]] push for the parliament to seize greater control over commerce, defense, and taxation from the [[Council of Four]]. This "[[Shadow Parliament]]" works to silence politicians who oppose their scheme.<ref name="AiF-p225">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|225}}</ref>

{{Yearbox/misc}}
* [[Myrna Nor]] and [[Powell Niccam]] identify the [[lost library of Lethchauntos (Dalelands)|lost library of Lethchauntos]] in the [[Dalelands]] as the likely location of ''[[The Nathlum]]''.<ref name="LLoL-p227">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn/The Lost Library of Lethchauntos|227}}</ref>
* Monster attacks along the edge of [[Cormanthor]] suddenly increase in frequency. Foresters believe the creatures to be coming out of the ruined [[Temple of Transmutation]] in [[Myth Drannor]].<ref name="AiF-p88">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|88}}</ref>
* [[Aberration]]s and [[undead]] begin attacking any who approach the [[Dallabad Oasis]] in the [[Calim Desert]].<ref name="AiF-p158">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|158}}</ref>
* The [[Calimemnon Crystal]] reappears as a "shooting star" that lands in the Calim Desert near Calimport. It is sought by both the [[marid]] Sultan [[Biha Babir]] of [[Maran Saya]] and by agents of Sultana [[Songal]] of Calimshan.<ref name="AiF-p159">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn|159}}</ref>
